title: Wireless AI Brain–Spine Interface Restores Natural Walking After Paralysis
whyItMatters: Built a wireless digital bridge between brain and spinal cord using real-time AI motor decoding, enabling a chronically paralyzed man to stand, walk naturally, and climb stairs by thought alone.
summary: Henri Lorach, Andrea Galvez, Jocelyne Bloch, Grégoire Courtine, and colleagues (EPFL, CHUV, CEA-Leti) reported in Nature (2023) the first wireless Brain–Spine Interface (BSI) restoring voluntary, natural gait after chronic spinal cord injury. Two implanted 64-channel WIMAGINE epidural cortical arrays record sensorimotor ECoG signals that an adaptive real-time machine-learning decoder translates into proportional stimulation commands sent to a 16-electrode lumbar spinal implant. Calibrated in minutes and stable for over a year at home, the BSI enabled a participant paralyzed for 12 years to stand, walk over uneven terrain, climb stairs, and regain partial neurological recovery even when the device was switched off.
technicalHighlights: Wireless digital bridge decoded real-time hip, knee, and ankle movement intentions from bilateral cortical ECoG to modulate epidural spinal stimulation.
Required only a few minutes of AI decoder calibration and remained stable across >40 neurorehabilitation sessions and independent home use over 1+ year.
Induced lasting neurorehabilitation gains: the participant regained ability to walk with crutches over ground even with the BSI turned off.
caveats: Demonstrated in a single clinical feasibility participant (n = 1) with an incomplete C5/C6 spinal cord injury; broader pivotal trials are required to evaluate safety and efficacy across complete injuries.

scoreRationale.foundational: First closed-loop wireless cortical-to-spinal digital bridge translating neural intent directly into natural multi-joint locomotion.
scoreRationale.ripple: Established the clinical neuroprosthetic blueprint for restoring mobility and upper-limb control after spinal cord injury and stroke.
scoreRationale.verification: Published in Nature with over a year of longitudinal home clinical data, though currently an n = 1 feasibility study.
scoreRationale.velocity: Reduced neural decoder calibration to minutes while triggering measurable biological neuro-recovery within months.
